subject: Metrics chorus: monthly KPI sync and exec asks
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Horizon Analytics <analytics@horizonfinance.com>
Date: 2028-11-01T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Metrics chorus: monthly KPI sync and exec asks

Team — attaching the month's dashboard and a small latency breakdown for context. High-level bullets first, then asks.

Highlights (last 30 days):
- Latency: 95th percentile (production, us-west) increased to ~280ms (from 210ms last month). P99 moved to 520ms during a burst on 10/26.
- Cost: unit cost per 1k tokens is up ~12% month-over-month driven by longer response lengths for the new sandbox customers.
- Uptime: service uptime for inference tier A is 99.92% (monthly target 99.95%). Two brief infra flaps on 10/26 contributed ~20m customer-facing downtime.
- Usage: daily active requests +18% (trial cohort from Horizon Finance and a paid small-burst customer).

Initial thoughts: the latency spike correlates with a kernel optimization deployed 10/25 plus an unexpected traffic pattern from Horizon's integration tests. The cost increase looks like a demand-side change (prompts longer) plus some increased sequential re-processing in a handful of larger batches.

Asks / action requests (QBR prep context):
1) Can infra roll back the 10/25 kernel change for a short canary tomorrow if we can't get a quick mitigation? Owner: @Jonas.
2) Product & Sales: confirm whether Horizon's trial usage pattern continues into the next billing cycle; if so we should model cost impact for QBR. Owner: @Laura (loop Horizon analytics).
3) Ops: create an incident ticket with latency traces and assign to runtime for root-cause. Add SUP-4532 to the QBR appendix. Owner: @Markus.
4) I'll update the exec dashboard with a 'what changed' slide and a short narrative for the QBR. Expect v4 by Friday.

Attachments: monthly_kpi_dashboard_v3.pdf (pdf), latency-breakdown-nov.csv (csv).

Thanks — Kim

--
Kimberly Park
VP, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-02T09:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Metrics chorus: monthly KPI sync and exec asks

Kim / team — quick follow-ups:

- I've started a quick trace pass on the 10/25 deployments. The kernel change increases some backend serialization for short sequences; it lines up with the latency bump. I don't yet see a full regression test failure but the telemetry shows higher tail latency for sequences <64 tokens.
- Rolling back the kernel change for a canary is doable but needs a short maintenance window for the canary host. If we do a rollback we should gate it behind a single-customer canary (Horizon) and monitor p95/p99 for 2 hours.

Action for my team: I'll open an internal incident and attach traces. If we decide to rollback, I'll coordinate the canary and add the exact maintenance window.

Jonas
